Rebuild, lowered from 3: SIM registration requires the ID card but no check against a register is stated (BDI-002, BDI-003), the test the first pass applied to Ghana and Tanzania. The 2023 statement of absence (BDI-001) is outside the window, so stage 1 cannot be claimed.

Rebuild: NPI authentication conditions SIM acquisition and public service platforms (BEN-010), and the fID QR app serves finance and education (BEN-006). The ePass app serves one procedure and is not a mobile ID.
Rebuild: the PKI e-signature platform was installed and staff trained in April 2025 (BFA-002). Nothing held says it is in use.
Rebuild: banks verify customers against the national citizen database through a national eKYC (BWA-003). The wider linkages date from 2015 and the PKI is not operational (BWA-006).
Rebuild: no evidence row is held on authentication.

Rebuild: the public administration e-signature system is in use and being extended across administrations (CIV-005), and MaPoste runs on a certified digital identity (CIV-007). Kept at 4 on the rung as worded; an e-signature system used by several bodies may be read as one service, which is stage 3.

Rebuild, raised from 3: secure e-signature is live in 37 of 40 administrations on AIGLE (CMR-003), a row the first pass counted as after its as-at. Staged on the rung as worded; read as one service, it is stage 3.
Rebuild: RDC-PASS launched in June 2026 and entered a first operational phase in September with enrolment agents (COD-011). No authentication in use is reported.

Rebuild: the only row is a 2023 electoral rule naming the ID card as a document to verify identity (COM-001), outside the window and not a digital service.
Rebuild: the Mobile Digital Key lets ID-card holders authenticate and sign online by app or SMS code (CPV-008), and SNIAC serves dozens of public and private bodies (CPV-012). Top rung.
Rebuild: Mobile ID, launched in February 2026, lets citizens authenticate and do procedures remotely (DJI-004), and partner administrations use its authentication (DJI-003). Top rung.

Rebuild: the national digital identity is used on the national services portal, the WADHIFATI platform and the civil-status platforms (DZA-006, DZA-002, DZA-010); the first pass cited an agreement instead. No app or wallet is named.

Rebuild, raised from 3: the Digital Egypt digital identity verifies users of the Public Prosecution portal and the social solidarity platform (EGY-005, EGY-007), so it serves several bodies. MOIEG-PASS, a selfie app, is in pilot only (EGY-001).
Rebuild: no evidence row is held on authentication.

Rebuild, raised from 4: the Fayda Wallet is in service for remote bank onboarding (ETH-011) and customers open accounts remotely with Fayda credentials (ETH-017), which the first pass did not read as remote proof. 150 enterprises use Fayda verification (ETH-016).
Rebuild: the World Bank-financed Gabon Digital programme includes a national digital identity with authenticated signatures and validations (GAB-003, GAB-004). Nothing is in service.
Rebuild: NIA biometric verification is used by GRA, NHIS, the Passport Office and banks (GHA-034). The Ghana Card e-wallet is announced, not in service (GHA-009).
Rebuild: ANDE is developing a PKI for electronic signatures (GIN-002); the voter-file convention cited before is a data source, not authentication. Nothing is in service.
Rebuild: the driver's licence system verifies applicants against the national ID (GMB-003). The eCRVS row describes a data link, so a service used by several bodies is not shown.
Rebuild: no evidence row is held on authentication.

Rebuild: over 800 organisations are integrated with IPRS for citizen verification (KEN-009). Nothing held says people prove who they are online with a mobile ID or wallet.
Rebuild: the Civil Service Agency uses the NIR e-verification portal (LBR-007). Other bodies' use is ordered or planned, not stated as live.
Rebuild: technical trials of eKYC against the biometric digital identity have begun with the Central Bank and banks (LBY-001). No service is reported live.
Rebuild: digital ID cards are listed among eKYC frameworks with financial use cases (LSO-003). Wider use is a pilot or a work plan (LSO-001, LSO-004).
Rebuild: the Mon e-ID app is in use with 2.5 million active users (MAR-015, MAR-009), adopted by several ministries and agencies (MAR-014). Top rung.

Rebuild, lowered from 3: DPI Map records in June 2025 that NINA has no digital authentication function (MLI-003), and the later rows take the NINA with no check against it stated (MLI-001, MLI-002). Stage 1 rests on that statement of absence.

Rebuild: SCDM e-signatures are used by more than 500 public and private institutions (MOZ-007), and the mobile digital ID is still in procurement (MOZ-001). Kept at 4 on the rung as worded; an e-signature system used by several bodies may be read as one service, which is stage 3.
Rebuild: the Houwiyeti app holds a phone-stored digital ID verified by selfie for e-government login (MRT-007), and public and private services verify users through it (MRT-002). Top rung.
Rebuild: a mobile digital ID launched in 2024 (MUS-006), and MauPass authenticates citizens across government e-services, most recently the KOREK! app (MUS-004, MUS-009). Top rung.

Rebuild: the Nzika wallet, launched on 16 September 2026, lets citizens present verified credentials to reach services (MWI-028), and NRB e-KYC serves banks, mobile money, SIM and utilities (MWI-012). Top rung.
Rebuild: the national PKI launched in August 2026 (NAM-005) and social grants use electronic identity verification (NAM-001). The e-ID for government and private use was still to launch (NAM-006).
Rebuild: WURI is building a population register to authenticate service users, and an e-ID card is under MoU (NER-001, NER-003). Nothing is in service.

Rebuild, raised from 4: individuals use the NINAuth app to prove their identity for SIM, passport, tax and financial transactions (NGA-006, NGA-037), which the first pass did not read as remote proof. The same rail serves telecoms, tax, banking and immigration (NGA-003).

Rebuild: identity verification against the national ID serves hospitals, government agencies and businesses across about 200 services (RWA-008). The phone-held Single Digital ID is being phased in to 2027 (RWA-004).
Rebuild: the SudaPass app holds a certified digital identity that signs binding transactions (SDN-012), and a bank verifies customers remotely through it (SDN-001). Top rung.

Rebuild: the e-Sénégal app authenticates users on the NIN for its procedures (SEN-001), and APPEL e-procurement uses strong authentication and e-signature (SEN-004). Neither is shown as one service used by several bodies.
Rebuild: the NCRA verification platform is used by financial and telecoms companies among others (SLE-023, SLE-006). Verifiable credentials are only at MoU (SLE-019).
Rebuild: the eAqoonsi app carries the national ID as a legally valid digital credential, obtained remotely (SOM-008, SOM-011), and over 100 services use the national ID system (SOM-017). Top rung.

Rebuild: a MOSIP-based digital ID and e-signature service are being built (STP-002, STP-001), and the citizen portal launched in March 2026 is built for ID login. The digital ID was still being implemented, so the login is not shown in use.
Rebuild: banks can check the civil registry to verify identity (SWZ-002). The national e-KYC was still to roll out (SWZ-001).

Rebuild, raised from 3: SeyID, validated by a video check against the civil status system, gates government e-services (SYC-004) on a portal hosting all government entities' systems (SYC-002). Its ID-Wallet is shown holding a driving licence, not as a way to prove identity online (SYC-001).
Rebuild: ANATS and Airtel signed in May 2026 for ANATS to verify subscriber data (TCD-001). No check is reported live.

Rebuild: Mobile ID, with over 450,000 holders, gives access to online services and e-signature (TUN-017), and E-Houwiya is integrated by many bodies and banks (TUN-016). Top rung.
Rebuild: 147 public and private institutions are connected to NIDA (TZA-008). Nothing held names a mobile ID or wallet.
Rebuild: UGHub connects NIRA's registry to over 150 ministries and agencies, banks and telecoms (UGA-022). Nothing held names a mobile ID or wallet.
Rebuild: Home Affairs verification is used by banks, mobile operators, insurers, SASSA and the justice cluster (ZAF-002, ZAF-013). The MyMzansi credential is a prototype (ZAF-017).
Rebuild: the FISP e-voucher uses eKYC verification in all 116 districts (ZMB-001), though what it checks against is not named. The PKI and ZamSign are under way (ZMB-003, ZMB-004).
